Invoicing & payments tools for Plumbers

Tools that help plumbers with invoicing & payments. Turning completed work into invoices, chasing payment and reconciling the books.

Where Invoicing & payments goes wrong for Plumbers

Domestic plumbing is often settled on site, and card payment on the day is the norm. Chasing payment later is awkward when the customer already considers the job finished.

What Plumbers jobs really involve

Plumbing work is mostly reactive — emergency callouts, narrow arrival windows and customers who want a price before you have seen the job. Speed of quoting and answering the phone tends to decide who wins the work.

Frequently asked questions

Which invoicing & payments tools work best for plumbers?

The three that fit best here are Joist (Solo contractors and small crews who mainly need to quote and get paid), Housecall Pro (Home service businesses that want one app covering booking through to payment), Jobber (Owner-operators and small crews moving off paper and spreadsheets). Start with the one whose description matches your crew size, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does invoicing & payments software cost for plumbers?

Across the 9 tools on this page, 2 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices change often, so treat the figures here as indicative and confirm on the vendor site.

Why does invoicing & payments cause problems for plumbers specifically?

Domestic plumbing is often settled on site, and card payment on the day is the norm. Chasing payment later is awkward when the customer already considers the job finished.

Can I quote a plumbing job from a photo?

Enough to give a range, not a fixed price. Most plumbers use photos to qualify the job and decide whether the visit is chargeable, then confirm the number on site before any work starts.
